newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Iron ore resource confirmed at Australia's Gawler.
newsitem.headline: Iron ore resource confirmed at Australia's Gawler.

text.p: Eight iron ore deposits, totalling 850 million tonnes, had been delineated to feed the proposed A$500 million South Australian Steel and Energy project (SASE), the South Australian said.

The SASE project, in the state's prospective Gawler Craton, involves the government with joint venture partners Meekatharaa Minerals Ltd, Ausmelt Ltd, and two Indonesian companies, PT Krakatau Steel and PT Maritosa Coalindo.
South Australia Mines Minister Stephen Baker said the state's mines department had concluded a highly successful A$2 million exploration program.

"Also associated with the iron ore deposits, which are located around 120 km south of Coober Pedy, are significant indications of gold and base metals further highlighting the extensive mineral potential of the Gawler Craton," he said in a statement.

Baker said eight separate iron depsoits had been defined within the Hawks Nest and Giffen Well prospects and inferred and indicated resources totalling 850 million tonnnes of magnetite ore grading 35 percent iron to a nominal depth of 130 metres had been outlined, he said.
Geophysical modelling indicated the iron ore extended to greater depths, indicating the existence of a much larger resource, he said.
